newsitem.title: USA: Seattle stadium plan leads in latest poll.
newsitem.headline: Seattle stadium plan leads in latest poll.

text.p: A massive advertising blitz appears to be persuading voters to support billionaire Paul Allen's plan to build a publicly financed football stadium in downtown Seattle, according to a poll published Wednesday.

The proposed $425 million open-air professional football and soccer stadium was backed by 48 percent of likely voters in the latest poll, compared with 44 percent who oppose it, according to the poll published in the Seattle Post-Intelligencer less than a week before the June 17 special election.

That compares with 56 percent who opposed the plan and 38 percent who supported it in a poll taken just a month ago, before the election vehicle backed by Allen began flooding the state's airwaves with advertisements touting the benefits of the new stadium, which would replace the 21-year-old Kingdome.

Allen, co-founder of Microsoft Corp. whose $13 billion stake in the software giant makes him the nation's third-wealthiest individual, holds an option to buy the Seattle Seahawks football team that expires July 1.

Allen has said he will walk away from the deal, clearing the way for the current owners to try to move the team out of town, unless the state's voters adopt a plan to provide $325 million in public financing for the proposed new stadium.
The remaining $100 million would be provided by Allen and through the sale of seat licenses.

Allen, who reportedly has never voted in an election, has contributed $4.8 million toward the pro-stadium campaign, more than Republican Sen. Slade Gorton raised in his 1994 re-election campaign, the newspaper reported.
Stadium opponents have raised about $200,000 for their campaign so far.
The survey of 800 likely voters was conducted for the newspaper and KOMO-TV and has a margin of error of 3.5 percentage points, the newspaper said.
